To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed an improved method for RNA extraction from plants using commercial reagents.

the addition of 1% (v/v) of β-mercaptoethanol to the lysis buffer and the use of the PEG-8000 solution for the precipitation of RNA from plants with high content of phenolic compounds and polysaccharide significantly improves the quality and quantity of RNA obtained from different tissues of plants rich in secondary compounds.
we present an improved method for isolation of high quality RNA from plants using commercial reagent kits, which allows the isolation of RNA from different types of plant tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of RNA isolation from plants rich in phenolics, anthocyans and polysaccharids.
the development of a simple, rapid, and inexpensive method of isolating RNA from plants rich with secondary metabolites.
the improvement of RNA extraction from plants with high content of phenolic compounds, anthocyanin and polysaccharide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the described method can be applied for the extraction of RNA from plants with a high concentration of phenolics and polysaccharide, and it can be used for the preparation of RNA from different types of plant tissues.
the described method is a simple and efficient method for the isolation of high-quality RNA from plant tissues rich in secondary metabolite compounds.

the described method of RNA extraction using commercial reagent kits can be successfully used for isolation of high-quality RNA from plants rich with secondary metabolites and is applicable to a variety of tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RNA isolation from the plant tissues using the commercial reagent kits can be improved with the use of a simple modification.

the use of commercial reagent kits for RNA extraction from plants rich in phenolics, anthrocyanins and polysacharides can be improved by the addition of a simple step of centrifugation of the supernatant after the first extraction step and the use of a different buffer for the second extraction step.
the modified RNA isolation method is a simple, rapid and cost-effective procedure for the isolation of high-quality RNA from plants rich of secondary metabolites.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of 1% polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) to the extraction buffer and the addition of 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol (β-ME) to the extraction and wash buffer significantly improved the quality and yield of RNA.
the use of commercial kits for RNA extraction from plant material rich in secondary metabolities is possible, but the protocol should be adapted.
the use of commercial reagents for RNA isolation is a simple, efficient and low-cost alternative to traditional methods.
